notes: Action feedback: every action now runs through one global action manager (frontend/js/actions.js) with the states idle → processing → success/completed/failed/cancelled. The control that started it shows the work immediately, is snapshot/restored exactly (markup, icon and accessibility attributes), cannot fire twice, and always returns to its normal state — success, error, timeout, abort or navigation away.

Buttons: ui.setButtonLoading no longer rewrites `disabled` or loses the original markup. Two actions on the same control are reference counted, so one finishing cannot re-enable or relabel the other, and a page that owns a control's disabled state keeps ownership of it.

Notifications: exactly one confirmation per real outcome, deduplicated across double clicks, duplicated WebSocket events and repeated polls; success toasts are green with a check icon, errors carry the backend detail, and a burst is capped so it cannot cover the screen on a phone.

Long-running work: training, uploads and evaluation are tracked operations with their real backend state (requested/queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled), real progress where the backend reports it, start and finish times, and a persistent Operation centre that survives a reload. A reload marks interrupted client-side operations as cancelled instead of leaving them Running forever.

Uploads: the dataset upload reports creating → transferring (real tus/bytes progress) → verifying and registering, then confirms only after the backend has verified the stored object, refreshes the dataset list and updates dashboard state. A queue that cannot be persisted no longer leaves the Upload button stuck.

Training: the monitor reconciles the job status from the create response, WebSocket events and the polling fallback through one idempotent path, so a job that completes while the page is open reports Completed once, with its real final metrics, and stops its indicators; a failed job no longer leaves the control mid-action.

Interaction performance: navigation no longer waits for a page's data. The router starts every navigation immediately and only the newest one may paint, so a click during a slow request is honoured instead of being swallowed.

Requests belong to the page that started them: leaving a page aborts its in-flight calls and a late response can never overwrite the page you are on. Cancelled requests are reported as cancelled, never as a backend failure or an error toast.

Read cache with request de-duplication (frontend/js/api.js): collection reads are cached for API_CACHE_TTL_MS (20 s) per signed-in user, identical concurrent reads share one request, every write and every 'changed' event invalidates the cache, and a manual Refresh bypasses it. Measured: 30 API calls per navigation cycle before, 9 now, 4 on a repeat cycle.

Large lists render in bounded pages with one delegated listener instead of one per row, and list cards no longer register AOS observers. Measured on 300 models / 500 datasets: Models page 1089 ms → 178 ms, Datasets 858 ms → 104 ms, DOM 19 435 → 1 094 nodes.

Instant press feedback and duplicate-action protection: a delegated pointerdown listener shows .is-pressed before any handler runs, buttons show aria-busy spinners, and start/pause/resume/stop run once even if tapped repeatedly.

Live training metrics are coalesced into one animation frame, the log panel is capped at 300 lines, live charts update without the entry animation, and leaving the Training page destroys its Chart.js instances.

Performance instrumentation (frontend/js/perf.js): first paint, time-to-interactive, per-route navigation time, per-endpoint API latency, long tasks, memory and failures via CORPUS_PERF.print(), CORPUS_APP.getDiagnostics().perf, or ?debug=1. Route paths only; no tokens or user data.
Backend: objective 'newest N' windows for training metrics and logs (?limit=), so a long run no longer streams its entire history on every poll; guarded by backend/tests/test_api_performance.py.

Android file picker: use a visible native file input, keep its associated label tappable, remove the transparent overlay and synthetic click fallback, and retain queue validation and IndexedDB persistence.

Authentication fix: a backend 401 no longer signs the user out. The session is cleared only when Supabase itself has no session; when the backend rejects a token that Supabase still holds (expired access token, mismatched publishable key, misconfigured backend) the API raises a 'backend rejected your session' error and keeps the user signed in (frontend/js/api.js).

Navigation fix: Supabase re-emits SIGNED_IN when it restores or refreshes a stored session (page reload, token refresh, returning from the Android file picker). Only an interactive sign-in from this page now navigates to Dashboard; restored sessions re-render the current route instead (frontend/js/auth.js).

Upload reliability: uploads have a real timeout (CORPUS_CONFIG.UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, default 10 minutes instead of the 15 s JSON request timeout), refresh the access token once and retry the same dataset record on 401, and report explicit network/timeout/401/413/503 messages that state the dataset record is kept for retry (frontend/js/api.js).

Backend: the synchronous Supabase Storage SDK calls (dataset upload, dataset preview download, training dataset download, checkpoint/tokenizer upload) run in a worker thread instead of blocking the event loop, so a large transfer no longer stalls health checks, token refreshes or dataset listing for other requests.

Backend: if the dataset_files metadata write fails after the bytes reached storage, the object is deleted again and the dataset is marked failed — private storage never keeps uploads the database does not know about, and the API never reports success for a file it cannot serve.
howToVerify: GET <frontend-url>/version.json — the deployed buildId must equal the buildId committed in frontend/version.json on main.
